QF.id: AIFM CIII Governance and Due Diligence_15

question.text: When is an external member of the Investment Committee of a Cat III AIF NOT required to secure fresh consent from 75% of investors (by value) for their appointment?

answer.text: Whenever the AMC management unilaterally decides.
When the investor has a family relation with the proposed member.

When their name was already disclosed in the PPM or fund-document at the time of on-boarding investors; also for ex-officio members like Sponsor/Sponsor Group/Investment Manager Group changes in official capacity.

explanation.text: The Logic: Per SEBI Circular (June 25, 2021), external IC members whose names ARE disclosed in PPM/fund document at on-boarding do not need fresh 75% consent. Also, consent is not required for change in ex-officio external members (Sponsor, Sponsor Group, Investment Manager Group, or investors in their official capacity). The Trap: One distractor ignores investor rights; another overstates the threshold; another invents a family-tie exemption. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C and XIX-D test the same carve-out. Important disambiguation: the 75% test is by VALUE of investment (not by number of investors). Manager's Pro-Tip: When drafting the PPM for a new Cat III fund, list ALL known external IC members + a named alternates panel — this pre-disclosure inoculates you against the 75%-consent requirement for later substitutions from that panel.
